reader.requirement: At --std 85, FUNCTION VARIANCE of one or more class-numeric arguments returns the square of the population standard deviation: the sum of the squared deviations from the arithmetic mean, divided by the number of values. The arguments can be items, literals, expressions, or table references with ALL subscripts (an ODO table at its current count).

edition-consulted.switches: D8 window: sig.IntroducedIn (85 on the catalog row) > ctx.Edition.DialectLevel raises COBOL1502, RemovedIn raises the removal error; at --std 85 neither fires

ConstructRegistry numeric-function-identifier-operand-2002: below 2002 a numeric/integer function written where an identifier stands (MOVE, DISPLAY) is refused COBOL0900; a function inside an arithmetic expression is not screened

the OPTIONS paragraph (so ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-*) is refused below 2002, so NumericRenderer#StandardDecimal is false at 85 and the renderer takes its native arm, the same arm 2023 takes with no OPTIONS paragraph

reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel/Edition/CobolVersion over IntrinsicRenderer.cs and src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/Intrinsics: no hits. The value path's only switch is num.StandardDecimal (the ARITHMETIC mode), which 85 cannot reach.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for the returned value: var1.cob prints the same output at --std 85 and 2023. Use as an identifier operand is refused only at 85.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses cover the exact-intake cancellation case and native equivalent-expression values. Only the probes exercise ALL over one- and two-dimensional tables, ODO tables at their current count, negative and scaled COMP arguments, and size error.

reader.notes: An all-fixed-point list goes to VarianceExact. It forms (n·Σd² − (Σd)²)/n² exactly on shifted integers and divides once, which gives the population variance: the square of the quantity in the 1985 STANDARD-DEVIATION's RV2. A binary64 argument takes the double body, which uses the same formula. The value path consults no edition.
reader.at-2023: var1.cob prints the same output at --std 2023

refuter.evidence: Read CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs#Variance: the binary64 body is two-pass (mean, then sum of (x-mean)^2 / n), so no cancellation. VRF.cob/VRD.cob at 85 = 2023: 100000000.1/.2/.3 exact, via NUMVAL, via MEAN, via expressions -> 0.006666666; SQRT(1E16), SQRT((1E8+1)^2), SQRT((1E8+2)^2) (binary64 path) -> 0.666666666, four values -> 0.1875, STANDARD-DEVIATION -> 0.816496580; same values -> 0. VRB.cob: TE(ALL) with 0 -> 1.5, TE(ALL) TE(ALL) -> 2.25, ODO N=1 single and doubled -> 0 (RV3), 14/9 ROUNDED 1.555555556 / truncated 1.555555555. VARIANCE(0 999999997) into 9(18) = 249999998500000000 where the exact value is 249999998500000002.25: the result is narrowed to binary64 once; the 1985 rule asks only for 'the approximation of the variance' and leaves the precision to the implementor, so this is within the rule (noted, not overturning). cite.py: OK §1989:A.2.45.4 RV2; OK §1989:A.2.41.4 RV2 'This quantity is divided by the number of values'; OK §1989:A.2.45.4 RV3; OK §1989:A.2.3 (GR2).
